title: Abstract strict lower-tail vanishing from degreewise Hom bounds
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with a derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-injective resolutions, and exact countable products. Let $P$ be a class of objects of $\mathcal A$ containing every zero object and invariant under isomorphism. Fix $S\in D(\mathcal A)$ and $N\in\mathbf Z$. Assume that $\operatorname{Hom}(S,B[-q])=0$ for every $B\in P$ and every integer $q\le N$, where $B[-q]$ means the complex concentrated in degree $q$. If $L\in D(\mathcal A)$ has $H^q(L)\in P$ for every $q$ and $H^q(L)=0$ for every $q>N-1$, then every morphism $S\to L$ is zero. There is no lower bound on $L$. The cohomological convention is that of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category].

source.place: Left completeness, Milnor sequence, and Right term; existing generic source-library devissage

proof.text: First prove the bounded assertion by induction on the number of supported cohomological degrees. The one-degree case is isomorphic to its sole cohomology sheaf placed in that degree. For the induction step, the standard truncation triangle separates the highest cohomology layer; representable Hom exactness factors a morphism through the lower truncation once its image in the highest layer is zero. Apply the induction hypothesis to this factorization. This is the existing proved DerivedCategory.eq_zero_of_isGE_of_isLE and its single-degree base case.

Exact countable products and K-injective resolutions give the existing generic left-completeness theorem isHomotopyLimit_truncGECone: L, with its canonical quotient maps, is the homotopy limit of tau_ge(-n)L. Every truncation has homology in P, because P contains zero and is invariant under isomorphism.

The bounded assertion applies both to each tau_ge(-n)L and to its shift by -1. Their upper bounds are N-1 and N, respectively; both have finite cohomology support and homology in P. Thus Hom from S to a tower term and from S[1] to that term vanish. The product universal property and exactness in the Milnor triangle force every map S to L to vanish. This is the fully proved existing DerivedCategory.eq_zero_of_isLE; the one-degree margin avoids an eventual-transition calculation.

proof_origin.place: eq_zero_of_isLE, and the proved bounded devissage lemmas immediately preceding it

lean.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_isLE {s : DerivedCategory C} (N : ℤ)
    (hvan : ∀ B, P B → ∀ n ≤ N, ∀ f : s ⟶ (singleFunctor C n).obj B, f = 0)
    (L : DerivedCategory C) (hL : homologyProperty P L) [L.IsLE (N - 1)] (f : s ⟶ L) :
    f = 0
